beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:storytelling, a hint of disbelief]In {1842|eighteen forty-two}, a British consul ^wrecked a royal tomb in Tunisia, just to take one ^stone.
[d:tension][act:the turn, wonder]Yet that stone let scholars read@present a lost African ^alphabet. [act:intrigued, a small smile][tune:fall]Or at least, its ^letters.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]The tomb stands at ^Dougga, in northern Tunisia. [p:0.93][act:plain, admiring]It's the Libyco-Punic mausoleum: about twenty-one metres of stone, as tall as a seven-storey building, in ^three tiers, from the second century BCE. [act:explaining, light]A mausoleum is simply a grand ^tomb.

[d:build][act:explaining, clear]Its inscription says the same thing ^twice, in two scripts. [act:precise]One is ^Punic, the language of Carthage, which scholars could already read@present. [act:the reveal][tune:fall]The other is ^Libyco-Berber, which nobody could. [act:a simple picture]Like one sentence printed in a language you know, and one you ^don't.
[d:build][go:4|0][act:storytelling, onward]Consul Thomas Reade had the stone pulled ^out, and the tomb came ^down. [act:plain]The stone went to the British ^Museum, in ^London.

[d:build][act:the decipherment, delighted][tune:rise]So how do you crack it? [act:explaining, clear]Names work like ^keys. [p:0.93][act:explaining, building]A name sounds the same in ^any script. [act:precise, building]Find a name in the Punic half, find it again in the other half, and you learn the ^sounds of its letters. [act:a simple picture]Like spotting a friend's name on a postcard written in a foreign ^alphabet. [p:0.9][act:the payoff, confident]Today, twenty-two of the twenty-four eastern signs are ^read@past.

[d:reveal][act:the twist, softer]But reading letters isn't reading a ^language. [p:0.93][act:careful, precise]The script writes no ^vowels. [act:playful, a simple picture]Rub the vowels out of English, and is it bird, bread, or ^bored? [act:careful]And most texts are ^names: this person, son of ^that one.

[d:build][act:quiet wonder]Its letters do live@verb on. [act:quiet wonder]The Tuareg script, ^Tifinagh, descends from it. [act:gentle][tune:fall]Yet the ancient language itself is still mostly ^silent.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]A lost alphabet ^cracked? [act:the verdict, confident][tune:fall]^*Established*, for its sounds. [act:open, honest]What those people actually ^said is still an open question.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:plain, the epilogue]The tomb was rebuilt in {1910|nineteen ten}, stone by stone. [act:the last word, quiet][tune:fall]But its most famous stone is still in ^London.
